artworks.title: Plaque with Medea's Murder of Absyrtus
artworks.description: Limoges enamel (Walters Art Museum): Medea kills her brother Absyrtus so she and Jason can escape — the Colchian prince as the cost of the Golden Fleece flight.

artworks.title: Medea Kills Her Brother Absyrtus
artworks.description: Carracci's Palazzo Fava frieze freezes the murder: Medea turns on Absyrtus — Aeëtes' son cut down so the Argo can outrun Colchian pursuit.

artworks.title: Absyrtus' Limbs Presented to His Father
artworks.description: Mannerist engraving (MET): Absyrtus' dismembered limbs returned to Aeëtes — the brother's body used as a delaying trail for the Colchian fleet.

artworks.title: Escape of Jason with Medea and the Death of Absyrtus
artworks.description: Early woodcut of the Argonaut escape: Absyrtus dies as Medea flees with Jason — the brother whose murder stains the fleece's afterstory.

artworks.title: Medea and Absyrtus (Four Seasons Mosaic, Antioch)
artworks.description: Antioch mosaic panel (Antakya Museum): Medea and Absyrtus named in tesserae — the Colchian siblings fixed in a Roman floor narrative of the Argonaut saga.

popCulture.title: Argonautica
popCulture.creator: Apollonius of Rhodes
popCulture.description: Apollonius places Absyrtus' death at the escape from Colchis — the brother Medea betrays so Jason can keep the fleece and outrun Aeëtes.

popCulture.title: Absyrtus
popCulture.description: Son of Aeëtes, brother of Medea — slain and (in many tellings) dismembered so the Argonauts can escape Colchis.
